checks: The initial whole-plane cap menu bounds every point of any compatible competitor, even if its own geometry differs. A larger feasible mass contradicts the minimizing normalized depth after restoring central volume, since positive barycentric weights force central positivity.

Each original facet persists under small erosion by its relative interior slack. Candidate vertices vary affinely and incidence stabilizes on a sufficiently short open interval. Persistent vertex active rows are old active rows at their limiting vertex, giving a finer erosion fan with the original facet rays.

Linearity on each fiber's own erosion fan is a linear subspace of the common simplicial fan chart and prevents new facet rays. The accepted finite support cone gives actual radial feasibility there. Common erosion preserves anchored Minkowski inclusion and has affine supports on that fan.

The fixed cap reduces each coincident owner derivative to min(delta,0) or max(delta,0). The finitely many facet branches are uniformly negative under erosion for each positive-mass active cap. Farkas gives the objective-one identity with the correct minus sign on active feasibility rows, and homogeneous dilation excludes zero total cap weight.

On each proper trace the constant and radial divergence formulas give the translation and dilation coefficients with section normal -u. At coincident inside and outside traces the paired section weights yield the same identities. Affine translations kill the chart rows and total volume derivative; dilation keeps the cap fixed and retains the signed threshold offset.
